thread:
jess: getting paged repeatedly for GPU health alerts over the last 45m. ECC corrected spikes + intermittent temp bursts on node gtx-23 and gtx-29. Paging noise is drowning out real customer-impact pages. starting this thread to coordinate a short-lived debounce and a plan for follow-up tuning.

mike: on it. I see the same in grafana: ECC corrected rate pops for ~30s, then quiet, repeat. Looks like flapping rather than sustained failures.

ops-bot: INCIDENT 2240001234 created: GPU_ECC_ALERT x7 in 1h, routing to #eng-oncall and paging rotation.

jess: customer-facing services show occasional latency bumps but no widespread 5xx. P95 token lat jumps correlate with the brief ECC bursts on gtx-23.

sanjay: quick triage: could be PCIe noise or a driver regression from the last runtime rollout. Any recent kernel or driver changes on those hosts?

mike: none in the last 24h for that rack. I pulled the node history: gtx-23 was restarted by kube due to an OOM job yesterday, but nothing else.

lee: suggest we debounce the alert and add a short for: window so flapping doesn't page. Also add a dedupe path to send repeated flaps to a quieter channel instead of pager.

jess: agreed. Immediate mitigation: 1) mute pager for this alert class with a short dedupe policy, 2) add a temporary for: 10m to the Prometheus rule, 3) create a dashboard panel for ECC transient rate and thermal correlation. Anyone object?

tayla: no objections. i'll patch the alert and open a PR to prod-alerts, then trigger a hot reload. will also add the grafana panel.

mike: PR ready, will paste change here for visibility.

mike: ```yaml
- alert: GPU_ECC_Transient
  expr: increase(node_gpu_ecc_corrected_total[5m]) > 0
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: ECC corrected bursts on GPU
```

mike: also changing routing: severity warning -> send to #eng-oncall-watch (no pager). Critical stays paged.

jess: good. tayla, can you deploy and confirm hot reload? If hot reload fails, fallback plan = mute pager for 30m and rely on manual checks.

ops-bot: applying alert rule update (deploy user tayla).

ops-bot: alertmanager config updated: route GPU_ECC_Transient -> channel #eng-oncall-watch, dedupe interval 15m.

tayla: update applied, hot reload succeeded. I also added a grafana panel on the gpu-health dashboard called "ECC burst + GPU temp" and pinned it to the incident channel. link: https://grafana.internal/d/abcd/gpu-health

jess: verifying metrics now. ECC pages have stopped paging us in the last 12m. seeing a couple of spikes in the panel but they don't trigger pager.

lee: next steps: open a follow-up ticket to investigate root cause (driver/firmware/neighbor-noise), add a permanent dedupe policy, and propose a more nuanced alert that looks at sustained ECC increase or correlates with VRAM errors and thermals. I'll take the postmortem action item.

sanjay: for the permanent alert we should consider two signals: sustained increase over 30m OR delta > threshold plus elevated GPU temp. Example query idea: increase(node_gpu_ecc_corrected_total[30m]) > 10 and avg_over_time(node_gpu_temp_celsius[30m]) > 75.

jess: capturing all this in the incident notes. we also need to notify customers if we see repeat latency hits tied to ECC; but right now no customer escalations.

mike: adding runbook snippet for on-call: when GPU_ECC flaps, check: 1) is it single node or multiple? 2) correlate with temp and p95 latency 3) check RAID/PCIe errors on host 4) consider temporary node drain if we see VRAM OOMs. sample drain command: ```bash
kubectl drain gtx-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```

jess: thumbs up. i'll do the handoff to the next oncall with notes: debounce applied, grafana panel added, follow-up ticket created (#INFRA-1452), owner lee. Please add any more context.

lee: noted. i put a comment in the ticket: schedule firmware check and run a short stress test on gtx-23/29 during maintenance window. also add a regression test for the runtime build that hit prod last week.

pagerbot: pager rotation updated. next oncall: mike -> tayla at 05:00 UTC handoff.

jess: thanks team. closing incident channel after handoff. will reconvene tomorrow AM to review data and decide permanent alert thresholds. :white_check_mark:
